headings.text: CA and trust (no CFSSL, no miniwerk)

blocks.html:
⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha and under rapid, breaking development. This page describes a moving target and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release — treat everything here as provisional, and do not rely on it for a production deployment.

This page covers deploying Deploy App on the newer Kubernetes platform, pvarki/opendefence-platform, which converts the Docker Compose stack into Kustomize manifests (base/ + overlays/<env>/). This platform is alpha. Unlike the legacy stack it has no miniwerk, and CFSSL is not the CA — certificate and trust material come from cert-manager + trust-manager + the **opendefense-pki** bundle. For the shared in-UI onboarding flow, see Operator quickstart.

How it is structured

Each application is split into base/ (environment-agnostic) and overlays/<env>/ (registries, pull secrets, hostnames, certificates, ingress). The top-level composition is phased under k8s/main/<env>/:

  • infra-phase1 — core operators (cloudnative-pg, cert-manager, external-secrets-operator)
  • infra-phase2 — trust-manager and the cluster issuers
  • monitoring — Grafana, Loki, Alloy, Prometheus
  • opendefense — the Deploy App workloads themselves (the opendefense-system namespace, including deployment/opendefense-rmapi, the core rmapi)

The task deploy flow applies these phases in order with readiness gates between them — do not bypass the sequencing.

Prerequisites (local)

  • kind — Kubernetes in Docker
  • kubectl
  • mise — tool version manager (recommended)

Tooling versions are pinned in mise.toml (helm 3, kind 0.31, kubectl 1.36, task 3, yq 4.53.2, zarf 0.76.0). Once mise is installed it auto-selects the right tool versions when you enter the project directory:

mise install   # install all pinned tools
mise trust     # trust the project's local mise config

Local deploy with kind

Bring up a kind cluster and deploy the whole stack:

task up        # create the kind cluster and deploy all resources
task down      # tear the cluster down
task           # list all available tasks

task up runs, in order: cluster:create (creates the opendefense-kind cluster from kind-config.yaml if absent), check-kubecontext, cluster:wait (waits for nodes Ready), then deploy:local. deploy:local applies the phased local kustomizations (k8s/main/local/*) with kubectl apply --server-side, waiting for each phase's controllers before continuing. Kustomizations that pull in Helm charts (traefik, trust-manager, external-secrets-operator) are rendered with --enable-helm.

The kind config maps the host ports the stack needs: 80/443 (Traefik web/websecure), 8089 and 8443 (TAK CoT streaming and native HTTPS via Traefik TCP passthrough), and the MediaMTX ports 1936 (RTMPS), 8322 (RTSPS), 8890 (SRT TCP+UDP), 9888 (HLS), 9889 (WebRTC), 9996 (playback).

The local deploy flow looks like this:

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
    A["task up"] --> B["cluster:create"]
    B --> C["check-kubecontext"]
    C --> D["cluster:wait"]
    D --> E["deploy:local"]
    E --> P1["infra-phase1"]
    P1 --> P2["infra-phase2"]
    P2 --> P3["monitoring"]
    P3 --> P4["opendefense"]

blocks.html:
Ingress: Traefik

Ingress is handled by Traefik (with IngressRoute resources and TCP passthrough for the TAK ports). It replaces the legacy nginx front door. Per-environment routes and certificates live in each service's overlays/<env>/, not in base/.

CA and trust (no CFSSL, no miniwerk)

Certificate issuance and trust distribution use Kubernetes-native operators:

  • cert-manager issues certificates.
  • **opendefense-pki** (k8s/opendefense-pki/) defines the CA chain: a CA cert, CA issuer, the OpenDefense CA, an intermediate CA, and a trust bundle.
  • trust-manager distributes the trust bundle across the cluster.

The core rmapi is wired to cert-manager rather than CFSSL via its environment, for example:

Do not document CFSSL or miniwerk as part of this platform — they belong to the legacy Docker Compose stack only.

Not yet documented. The local opendefense-system base still contains a miniwerk job configured for mkcert (MW_MKCERT=true) for local cert bootstrapping. Whether that is a transitional local-only artifact is still to be written up here. The canonical CA/trust path on this platform is cert-manager + trust-manager + opendefense-pki; Let's Encrypt-style miniwerk certificate provisioning is not part of it.

Other supporting operators

The platform also runs cloudnative-pg (PostgreSQL), keycloak-operator, external-secrets-operator, projectcontour, longhorn (storage), and the prometheus/grafana operators, each as its own k8s/<component>/ Kustomize unit composed in via k8s/main/<env>/.

Cloud deploy with Zarf

For an external cluster, build a Zarf package from the cloud overlays and deploy it. The build renders the same four cloud phases and bundles their manifests:
task zarf:package:cloud

This writes zarf-package-opendefense-cloud-<arch>-1.0.0.tar.zst to the repo root (default architecture amd64; override with ZARF_ARCHITECTURE=arm64). Then deploy against your cluster's kubeconfig, supplying the deploy-time hostname. The KUBECONFIG below points at whatever kubeconfig your target cluster gave you — e.g. when in Azure that might be a k3s-azure.yaml, but the target cloud is just an example; any reachable cluster works:

KUBECONFIG=k3s-azure.yaml zarf package deploy \
  zarf-package-opendefense-cloud-amd64-1.0.0.tar.zst \
  --set OPENDEFENSE_HOST=example.dev.pvarki.fi --confirm

OPENDEFENSE_HOST is a deploy-time Zarf variable; cloud overlay resources reference ###ZARF_VAR_OPENDEFENSE_HOST### and Zarf substitutes it at deploy time. The package deploys in the same phased order as task deploy:cloud: infra-phase1 (waits for CNPG, cert-manager, external-secrets), then infra-phase2 (cluster issuers, waits for trust-manager), then monitoring, then opendefense. See zarf/cloud/README.md for build internals (including YOLO mode via ZARF_YOLO=true).

First admin invite code

Generate the first admin invite code from the core rmapi. On this platform that is deployment/opendefense-rmapi in the opendefense-system namespace:

kubectl exec -it -n opendefense-system deployment/opendefense-rmapi -- \
  rasenmaeher_api addcode

Not yet documented. The exact in-container invocation on k8s — whether the virtualenv must be activated first (e.g. source /.venv/bin/activate && rasenmaeher_api addcode, as in some legacy modes) — is still to be written here. The command name (rasenmaeher_api addcode) and target deployment are settled; only the shell wrapper is open.

Then follow the shared in-UI flow in Operator quickstart. For ongoing operations on this platform see Day-2 operations (Kubernetes); for development against a running platform (mirrord), see Develop Deploy App.
